benchmarks.task_description:
fix(llm): list only the DeepSeek GGUF quantizations that exist

### Description

Four DeepSeek ggufv2 specs list quantizations that their Hugging Face repos do not have as loadable files:

- **deepseek** and **deepseek-chat** 67B (`TheBloke/deepseek-llm-67b-chat-GGUF`): Q6_K and Q8_0 were uploaded as raw byte chunks (`deepseek-llm-67b-chat.Q6_K.gguf-split-a` / `-split-b`). They have to be concatenated by hand, so the resolved `deepseek-llm-67b-chat.Q6_K.gguf` does not exist.
- **deepseek-coder-instruct** 7B (`LoneStriker/deepseek-coder-7b-instruct-v1.5-GGUF`): there is no Q4_0 or Q5_0 file.
- **deepseek-coder** 7B (`dagbs/deepseek-coder-7b-base-v1.5-GGUF`): there is no Q5_0 file.

Launching any of these fails at download. This PR drops them from the specs, and `gen_docs.py` updates the four model pages.

### Test

The new `xinference/model/llm/tests/test_deepseek_gguf_quantizations.py` checks each spec's quantizations against the single-file quantizations in its repo. It fails on `main` and passes with this change. The repo file lists were checked again today through the Hugging Face tree API. `pre-commit run` on the changed files passes.

benchmarks.task_description:
fix(hawk): refuse on the runner any model the run did not declare to Hawk

**The bad scenario:** a Hawk run whose protocol comes from a setting only the Hawk runner checks out (`--hawk-arg use=<setting>@<ref>`). Your machine can't load that protocol, so the launcher declares to Hawk only the roles it can see. If the runner then binds a model of its own, nothing stops it. Hawk decides who may see a run's results from the declared models, so that model's results get past Hawk's access check. Jev is one example: the runner binds its default `jev` role when it resolves the protocol, and without middleman that is an undeclared call on your own OpenRouter key.

**Fix:** the launcher sends the runner the exact model list it declares to Hawk (`CONTROL_TOWER_HAWK_MODELS`, for eval sets and scans). `make_role_model` builds every role-bound model on the runner, and now refuses any model that isn't on the list, naming the role and the model. This covers every role by construction, not monitor by monitor. Ordinary monitors weren't leaking, because they answer on roles the launcher already bound.

**Jev:** this drops the `CONTROL_TOWER_HAWK_MIDDLEMAN` refusal that linuxarena/control-tower#2711 added to `TypeSafe`. Jev reaches its model only through a role, and `typesafe/…` can never be declared to Hawk. So under Hawk, Jev is refused either at launch or on the runner, with or without middleman. One case loses that refusal: a runner pinned with `use=control-tower@<ref>` to a version from before this PR, which ignores the list.

**Not covered:** models built by name with a direct `get_model` instead of a role binding, such as env code's `generate` in `environments/remote/sample.py`. Inspect's `on_before_model_generate` hook can't be the check point, because Inspect logs and swallows exceptions raised in hooks.

**Checked:** `make check` green.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

benchmarks.task_description: Fix EXIF jpeg detection: read more than just the first APP1 segment APP1 segments can also hold XMP data. The CPU JPEG decoder used the first APP1 segment whatever its payload, so a JPEG with an XMP segment before its EXIF segment lost its EXIF orientation. We now use the first APP1 segment starting with `"Exif\0\0"`, like Pillow and like the nvJPEG path already did. get_image_metadata() is updated to match. Also adds tests checking that `decode_image() `and `get_image_metadata()` agree with Pillow's `ImageOps.exif_transpose()`, which later fixes extend. --- Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬

benchmarks.task_description:
fix(operations.iptables): quote user input in iptables commands

## Describe the bug
`iptables.chain` and `iptables.rule` interpolate `table`, `chain`, `policy` and every rule field (protocol, source, destination, interfaces, jump, log_prefix, to_destination/source/ports) into the iptables/ip6tables commands with f-strings and `" ".join`.

This PR fixes it by composing the command(s) with `StringCommand` and wrapping the user-supplied values in `QuoteString` (from `pyinfra.api`). Part of the #1760 shell-injection hardening (item 6).

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior, please include where possible:

+ Operation code & usage

```python
from pyinfra.operations import iptables

iptables.chain(chain='x; reboot')
```

+ Target system information: any POSIX target (Linux/BSD).
+ Example using the `@docker` connector (helps isolate the problem): `pyinfra @docker/alpine deploy.py`.

## Expected behavior
Every user value is shell-escaped. `extras` stays raw as it is a multi-token passthrough of extension args. The crafted input is passed to the program as a single literal argument instead of being interpreted by the shell. A new injection fixture covers this.

## Meta
+ Include output of `pyinfra --support`: v3.9.2 (branch `3.x`), Python 3.10+.
+ How was pyinfra installed (source/pip)? Source (this branch).
+ Include pyinfra-debug.log (if one was created): n/a, this is a code fix covered by fixtures.
+ Consider including output with `-vv` and `--debug`: n/a. Verified with `scripts/dev-test.sh` and `scripts/dev-lint.sh`.

benchmarks.task_description:
Reject an empty languages set on a custom check oracle

`CustomCheckOracle`'s `languages` validator checked `value and not len(value)`, which no set satisfies, so an empty `languages` set was accepted. The check is now `value is not None and not value`: an empty set raises `At least one language is required.` when the suite is loaded, instead of every submission later getting "This test suite is not solvable in <Language> … code is only provided for set()". `None` (no restriction) and non-empty sets behave as before.

Only JSON test suites can hit this: the DSL already turns `languages: []` into `None` (`translate_parser.py`), unchanged here.

`test_custom_check_oracle_accepts_languages` (added in #897) asserted that `languages=set()` is accepted, the case this fixes; that line is dropped.

Closes #898.

## Manual testing

1. Check out `bug/898-empty-custom-check-languages` in the devcontainer.
2. Run `pytest tests/test_suite.py -k custom_check`: all pass. On `master`, `test_custom_check_empty_languages_raises` and `test_custom_check_empty_languages_in_json_raises` fail with "DID NOT RAISE".
3. In a Python shell: `from tested.testsuite import CustomCheckOracle, EvaluationFunction`, then `CustomCheckOracle(function=EvaluationFunction(file="e.py"), languages=set())` raises `ValueError: At least one language is required.`; with `languages=None` it builds.

<details>

+DATASETS = {
+    "MetaQA": {
+        "rag": "out/metaqa_rag_results/metaqa_{}_pure_.jsonl",
+        "baseline": "out/metaqa_baseline_results/metaqa_{}_baseline_no_rag.jsonl",
+    },
+    "WC2014QA": {
+        "rag": "out/wc14_rag_results/wc2014_{}_.jsonl",
+        "baseline": "out/wc14_baseline_results/wc2014_{}_baseline_no_rag.jsonl",
+    },
+}
+
+
+def load_jsonl(path):
+    with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
+        rows = [json.loads(line) for line in f if line.strip()]
+    return sorted(rows, key=lambda r: r["id"])
+
+
+def normalize_wc14(pred):
+    # Same normalization as src/eval_wc14_rag.py
+    return pred.rstrip().replace(" ", "_").lower().split(",")[0]
+
+
+def token_f1(pred, gold):
+    pred_tokens = pred.replace("_", " ").split()
+    gold_tokens = gold.replace("_", " ").split()
+    common = sum((Counter(pred_tokens) & Counter(gold_tokens)).values())
+    if common == 0:
+        return 0.0
+    precision = common / len(pred_tokens)
+    recall = common / len(gold_tokens)
+    return 2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall)
+
+
+def score_metaqa(rows):
+    # Per-question scores are already stored by src/eval_metaqa_rag.py
+    hits = [bool(r["top1_match"]) for r in rows]
+    em = [bool(r["exact_match"]) for r in rows]
+    f1 = [r["f1"] for r in rows]
+    return hits, f1, em
+
+
+def score_wc14(rows):
+    hits, f1, em = [], [], []
+    for r in rows:
+        pred = normalize_wc14(r["prediction"])
+        valid = [a.lower() for a in r["valid_answers"]]
+        hits.append(pred in valid)
+        em.append(pred == valid[0])
+        f1.append(max(token_f1(pred, a) for a in valid))
+    return hits, f1, em
+
+
+def mcnemar(a, b):
+    """McNemar test with continuity correction. Returns the two-sided p-value."""
+    only_b = sum((not x) and y for x, y in zip(a, b))
+    only_a = sum(x and (not y) for x, y in zip(a, b))
+    if only_a + only_b == 0:
+        return 1.0
+    chi2 = (abs(only_b - only_a) - 1) ** 2 / (only_a + only_b)
+    return math.erfc(math.sqrt(chi2 / 2))
+
+
+def significance(p):
+    if p < 0.001:
+        return "***"
+    if p < 0.01:
+        return "**"
+    if p < 0.05:
+        return "*"
+    return "n.s."
+
+
+def pct(values):
+    return 100 * sum(values) / len(values)
+
+
+def main():
+    for name, paths in DATASETS.items():
+        score = score_metaqa if name == "MetaQA" else score_wc14
+        rag_hits = {}
+
+        print(f"\n{name}")
+        print(f"{'Model':<10} {'Base H@1':>9} {'Base F1':>8} {'Base EM':>8} {'RAG H@1':>8} {'RAG F1':>7} {'RAG EM':>7}")
+
+        for key, label in MODELS:
+            base = score(load_jsonl(paths["baseline"].format(key)))
+            rag = score(load_jsonl(paths["rag"].format(key)))
+            rag_hits[label] = rag[0]
+            values = [pct(m) for m in base + rag]
+            print(f"{label:<10} " + " ".join(f"{v:>8.2f}" for v in values))
+
+        print(f"\n{name} McNemar (RAG Hits@1)")
+        print(f"{'Comparison':<20} {'Delta pp':>9} {'p-value':>10}  Sig.")
+
+        for (_, a), (_, b) in combinations(MODELS, 2):
+            delta = pct(rag_hits[b]) - pct(rag_hits[a])
+            p = mcnemar(rag_hits[a], rag_hits[b])
+            print(f"{a + ' vs ' + b:<20} {delta:>+9.2f} {p:>10.2g}  {significance(p)}")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

benchmarks.task_description:
CI: test every push that changes the code of a PR - issue #1752

> Before submitting, read the [contributing guidelines](CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [AI policy](AI-POLICY.md).

## What does this PR do and why?
Removes the "code of the PR unchanged" skip of #1749 (and its fallback, #1751), for the reasons raised in the review of haddocking/disvis#38:
- `git patch-id` ignores whitespace, so a push that only re-indents lines of the PR skipped the tests;
- after merging `main`, the PR together with the new `main` was not tested before merging.

The jobs depend again only on the `tj-actions/changed-files` filters. The `*.md` exclusions added in #1749 are kept and now also cover `docs/` (the only filtered path without one), so a change that only touches Markdown files does not run the tests. The docs build does not use `-W`, so a Markdown change cannot fail it.

## How was this tested?
- The re-indent case was reproduced in a test repository (same patch ID before and after).
- The workflow is the one from before #1749 plus the `*.md` exclusions (`git diff 8969933d3^ -- .github/workflows/ci.yml`).
- The workflow runs on this PR.

## AI assistance
Claude Code wrote the change and the checks above; I reviewed them.

## Checklist

- [ ] Tests cover the new and/or changed code
- [ ] Documentation updated if needed (also in the [haddock3 user-manual](https://github.com/haddocking/haddock3-user-manual)
- [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` updated for user-facing changes

## Related issues
Closes #1752

## Notes for reviewers

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
